sentences.text: Emiliasaura is an extinct genus of ornithopod dinosaurs from the Early Cretaceous of Argentina, containing only one known species, Emiliasaura alessandrii.
Research indicates that the known specimens of Emiliasaura belonged to subadult individuals that were still growing.
The genus name honors Emilia Ondettia de Fix, who founded the first museum in Las Lajas, while the species name honors Carlos Alessandri, the discoverer of the holotype specimen.
This dinosaur lived in an environment that included tree ferns and podocarp conifer trees.

The fossils were discovered by Carlos Alessandri in the summer of 2009 near Las Lajas, Argentina, and Emiliasaura alessandrii was formally described as a new genus and species in 2025 by Coria and colleagues.

Emiliasaura was initially identified as a rhabdodontomorph, which would make it the oldest known member of that clade, but later analyses placed it outside the Rhabdodontomorpha clade, instead classifying it as a styracosternan.

One phylogenetic analysis recovered Emiliasaura as the most basal member of the Rhabdodontomorpha, another study concluded that it likely belongs to a genus outside the Rhabdodontomorpha, and a third analysis identified it as the most basal member of the Rhabdodontomorpha.
Emiliasaura lived during the Valanginian age of the Early Cretaceous period, approximately 139 to 132 million years ago in what is now South America.
The fossil record for Emiliasaura spans from 137.05 to 132.6 million years ago.
It is debated whether Emiliasaura is a basal rhabdodontomorph or an early-diverging styracosternan within Dryomorpha.
